FALSE as stated, by explicit counterexample; see strongest_attack. The artifact's own operative hypothesis is 'q_*script-W is finite locally free and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change', and theorem_scope repeats that this is the whole of the 'standard CE equation-bundle open'. Under exactly that hypothesis the restriction r: q_*script-W -> pi_*W need not be surjective: from the degree-four CE Koszul resolution 0 -> O_X(-4) tensor q^*det F -> O_X(-2) tensor q^*F -> I_C -> 0, tensoring by script-W = O_X(2) tensor q^*F^vee and pushing down gives Rq_*(I_C tensor script-W) = End(F) concentrated in degree zero (all of q_*, R^1q_*, R^2q_* of O_X(-2) vanish on a P^2-bundle, the R^2 by relative duality with omega_{X/P^1}=O_X(-3) tensor q^*det E). Hence coker(r) injects into H^1(P^1,End F) with next term H^1(P^1, Sym^2 E tensor F^vee) = H^1 of q_*script-W, so on the equation-bundle open coker(r) IS EXACTLY H^1(P^1, End F), which vanishes iff F is fibrewise balanced. The attempt's stated reason, 'using H^1(X_b,O_{X_b})=0', is the wrong vanishing group: H^1 of the structure sheaf of a P^2-bundle over P^1 vanishes unconditionally and carries no information about surjectivity onto H^0(C,W).

True at balanced (6,6) but not established by the supplied argument. For F fibrewise O(4)+O(5) one has End F = O+O+O(1)+O(-1) with H^1=0, so r IS surjective there and the ambient/intrinsic cokernels do agree; I verified the bookkeeping with E=O(3)^3: h^0(X,script-W)=h^0(O(2)^6)+h^0(O(1)^6)=30, h^0(End F)=4, h^1(End F)=0, and 30-4+0=26=h^0(C,W). But this correct reason appears nowhere in the artifact: CLM-0064-8 is derived from CLM-0064-7, whose general form is false and whose fibrewise input is attributed to an SRC-0004 surjectivity statement that is not visible in the packet excerpt and is supported by the wrong vanishing. The conclusion is therefore not discharged by this artifact, only by a computation the artifact does not contain.

scope.generality: all degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl covers of P^1, any g
objects: CE equation bundle script-W = O_X(2) tensor q^*F^vee

finding_candidates.statement: For a degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl cover C in X = P(E^vee) over P^1 with relations bundle F and equation bundle script-W = O_X(2) tensor q^*F^vee, the ambient-to-curve restriction H^0(X,script-W) -> H^0(C,W) has cokernel canonically contained in H^1(P^1, End F), with cokernel of the inclusion mapping into H^1(P^1, Sym^2 E tensor F^vee); consequently on the CE equation-bundle open, where R^1q_*script-W = 0, the cokernel EQUALS H^1(P^1, End F). Proof: tensor the CE Koszul resolution 0 -> O_X(-4) tensor q^*det F -> O_X(-2) tensor q^*F -> I_C -> 0 by script-W and push forward; the O_X(-2)-twisted term has vanishing q_*, R^1q_* and R^2q_* on a P^2-bundle (R^2 by relative duality with omega_{X/P^1} = O_X(-3) tensor q^*det E), leaving Rq_*(I_C tensor script-W) = End(F) in degree zero. Since H^1(P^1, O(a)+O(b) tensor (O(-a)+O(-b))) vanishes iff |a-b| <= 1, the restriction is surjective exactly on the fibrewise BALANCED locus. Balancedness of F is therefore a strictly stronger hypothesis than membership in the CE equation-bundle open, and any ambient-versus-intrinsic CE comparison must assume it explicitly.

finding_candidates.evidence: Solve 4g+12-4f_2 - n = 2g-2 for n; check f_1 < f_2 is exactly d_4 - n > 2g-2. Witness verified: bidegree (4,3) on P^1 x P^1 gives g = (4-1)(3-1) = 6, deg omega_C = 2*3+1*4 = 10, deg gamma_*O_C = -9 = -(g+3), deg omega_{C/P^1} = 10+2*4 = 18, and |omega_{C/P^1} tensor gamma^*O(-3)| = |O(2,0)|_C| of degree 6 and projective dimension 2, factoring through the Veronese conic.

scope.generality: degree-four CE data with the GEO-Z degree conditions

finding_candidates.statement: The GEO-Z standing degree conditions d_4 - n > 2g-2 and d_5 - n = 2g-2, when specialized to degree-four CE data with F = O(f_1)+O(f_2), f_1 < f_2, f_1+f_2 = g+3 and deg W_f = 4g+12-4f, are equivalent to n = 2g+14-4f_2 together with f_1 < f_2. They do NOT single out the balanced splitting type. For g = 6 they admit at least the two solutions (f_1,f_2,n) = (4,5,6) (balanced, the campaign case) and (f_1,f_2,n) = (3,6,2) (unbalanced), the latter realized by a smooth bidegree-(4,3) curve on P^1 x P^1 with its degree-four projection, which has gamma_*O_C = O + O(-3)^3, hence E = O(3)^3, and lies on a constant conic in P^2 x P^1, hence F = O(3)+O(6). For E = O(3)^3 the section condition H^0(Sym^2E(-f)) not zero forces f <= 6, so (4,5) and (3,6) are the only splitting types available there. Consequence for the campaign: a GEO-Z theorem whose intrinsic hypotheses are stated purely by degree inequalities silently quantifies over unbalanced tetragonal CE data, so any ambient CE clause appended to those hypotheses inherits the unbalanced cases and must either exclude them by an explicit balancedness hypothesis or prove them. This is the mechanism by which an artifact can list 'unbalanced splitting types' under not_covered while its stated theorem in fact asserts something about them (the discipline of FND-0101), and it is a concrete instance of the unbalanced-locus exposure recorded abstractly in FND-0091.

finding_candidates.evidence: Direct: the restriction sequence is 0 -> I_C tensor script-W -> script-W -> i_* W -> 0, whose connecting map lands in H^1(X, I_C tensor script-W). The unbalanced witness in FC-CE-AMBIENT-RESTRICTION-COKER-IS-H1-ENDF has H^1(X,O_X) = 0 and yet a 2-dimensional restriction cokernel.
finding_candidates.statement: Surjectivity of a fibrewise ambient-to-curve restriction H^0(X_b, script-W_b) -> H^0(C_b, W_b) is governed by H^1(X_b, I_{C_b} tensor script-W_b), not by H^1(X_b, O_{X_b}). For a P^2-bundle over P^1 the latter vanishes unconditionally and is therefore vacuous as a justification; the former equals H^1(P^1, End F_b) in the degree-four CE setting. Reviewers and provers should treat 'H^1(ambient, O) = 0' as a null citation in this context: it neither implies nor is implied by the required vanishing, and its appearance is a reliable signal that an ideal-sheaf twist has been dropped from a restriction-surjectivity argument.

strongest_attack: Strongest attack (succeeded, and it is what drives the verdict): the theorem asserts, as an unqualified conclusion under hypotheses that do not mention balancedness, that 'the restriction q_*script-W->pi_*W is surjective'. I attacked that clause by asking what actually obstructs it, and the obstruction is computable in closed form. On the CE equation-bundle open (R^1q_*script-W=0) one has coker(r) = H^1(P^1_b, End F_b) exactly, via the degree-four CE Koszul resolution of I_C tensored by script-W = O_X(2) tensor q^*F^vee, whose pushforward is End(F) in degree zero. So r is surjective precisely on the fibrewise balanced locus, and the artifact's hypothesis set does not impose that. Explicit witness, all hypotheses satisfied: k=C, B=Spec k, C a smooth curve of bidegree (4,3) on P^1 x P^1, g=(4-1)(3-1)=6, gamma the degree-four projection, n=2 with Gamma two distinct points. Then gamma_*O_C = O + O(-3)^3 (push 0->O(-4,-3)->O->O_C->0; only R^1 of the first term survives, = O(-3)^3), so E=O(3)^3 with deg E = 9 = g+3. The relative canonical map to P^2 is |omega_{C/P^1} tensor gamma^*O(-3)| = |O(2,0)|_C|, which factors C -> P^1 -> P^2 through the Veronese conic Q, so C lies in Q x P^1: one CE relative conic is constant, forcing F = O(3)+O(6), det F = O(9) = det E. Degrees: the HN filtration O(6) subset F dualises to d_4 = 4g+12-12 = 24 (sub) and d_5 = 4g+12-24 = 12 (quotient), so d_4-n = 22 > 2g-2 = 10 and d_5-n = 10 = 2g-2 — both standing degree hypotheses hold, with n=2 >= 1. Equation-bundle hypothesis holds: q_*script-W = Sym^2E tensor F^vee = O(3)^6 + O^6, so it is free of rank 12 with H^1 = 0 and trivially base-change-compatible over a field. Yet h^0(X,script-W) = 24+6 = 30, h^0(End F) = 6, h^0(C,W) = deg W + 2(1-g) = 36-10 = 26 (both graded degrees 24 and 12 exceed 2g-2 = 10, so H^1(C,W)=0), and h^1(End F) = h^1(O(-3)) = 2, with 30-6+2 = 26 and alternating sum 6-30+26-2 = 0 confirming the sequence. Hence coker(r) is 2-dimensional and r is NOT surjective. The clause is therefore false under its own hypotheses, which refutes the theorem_statement as written; and since tilde-phi = phi o r factors through a proper subsheaf, 'coker(tilde-phi) canonically isomorphic to coker(phi)' loses its only proof, with Fit_0(coker tilde-phi) contained in but not equal to Fit_0(coker phi) in general. Second attack (attempted, FAILED — the artifact holds): I tried hard to break Sections 3-4, the nonreduced-base identity Fit_0(coker Phi) = I_e, on four fronts — that i_xi^*J = (eps) only detects kappa-rational tangents; that the first Nakayama is run over O_{B,b} while the second is over O_{P,e(b)}; that the Poincare bundle is only unique up to a twist from P; and that the off-section vanishing might merely be a support statement. All four fail: kappa-rational tangents span the conormal fibre, both Nakayama applications are on finite modules over Noetherian local rings with the ideal inside the maximal ideal, the ambiguous twist becomes trivial after pullback to a local ring, and both inclusions are genuine ideal containments. Third attack (attempted, FAILED): the ranks and the balanced degree arithmetic (20/16, 26->12, deg N = 0) are all correct, and the canonical-filtration construction correctly avoids the global splitting hypothesis that FND-0097 warns about. Net: the intrinsic half of this artifact (Sections 2-7, CLM-0064-1 through CLM-0064-6) is sound and is the campaign-usable content; the ambient CE half is refuted in its stated generality and unproved even in the balanced case it needs. Minimal repair: add 'F fibrewise balanced' (equivalently H^1(P^1_b, End F_b) = 0) as a hypothesis of the ambient clause, and replace the H^1(X_b,O_{X_b})=0 citation with the End(F) computation. Note also that the artifact's own theorem_scope lists 'unbalanced splitting types' as not covered while the refuted clause quantifies over them — the FND-0101 discipline applied to this artifact.
theorem_statement: Let k be a field of characteristic zero, B a locally Noetherian k-scheme, pi:C->B a smooth proper morphism with geometrically connected genus-g fibres, and x_1,...,x_n:B->C pairwise disjoint sections with n>=1 and Gamma=sum x_i(B). Let 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 be an exact sequence on C with W_4,W_5 invertible, W locally free of rank two, and constant fibre degrees d_4,d_5 satisfying d_4-n>2g-2 and d_5-n=2g-2. Put phi:pi_*W->pi_*(W|Gamma), N=omega_{C/B} tensor W_5^vee(Gamma), P=Pic^0_{C/B}, a_N:B->P, and let e:B->P be the identity. Then Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e, so the intrinsic evaluation-failure scheme is exactly a_N^{-1}(e(B)); this equality commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change and represents relative triviality of N, and it descends along smooth atlases to locally Noetherian algebraic stacks. Now additionally suppose the data come from a degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl embedding i:C->X=P(E^vee) over P^1_B, with q:X->B, relations bundle F, script-W=O_X(2) tensor pullback(F^vee), W=i^*script-W, and B contained in the standard CE equation-bundle open on which q_*script-W is locally free and commutes with arbitrary base change. Let tilde-phi:q_*script-W->pi_*(W|Gamma) be the ambient CE equation-evaluation map. Then the restriction q_*script-W->pi_*W is surjective, coker(tilde-phi) is canonically isomorphic to coker(phi), and the ambient CE evaluation-failure scheme has the same ideal a_N^*I_e. For (g,n)=(6,6) and F fibrewise O(4) direct-sum O(5), the canonical filtration induced by O(5) tensor q_0^*q_{0*}(F(-5)) subset F has d_4=20,d_5=16, the intrinsic map has ranks 26->12, and both intrinsic and ambient CE failure are scheme-theoretically the locus where O_C(Gamma) is relatively isomorphic to W_5 tensor omega_{C/B}^{-1}. This theorem constructs and identifies GEO-Z on the balanced CE/configuration stack; it makes no assertion about the image, closure, components, dimensions, stabilizers, or unbalanced splitting types in M_{6,6}, which are assigned to C66-GEO-H0 and C66-GEO-COMP.
